meta.title: uvdrop — Offline-first uv launcher for everyday work
meta.description: Pass a folder, ZIP, or shared catalog entry, review packages that come along before anything runs, then start your Python app with uv and a dedicated .env — offline-friendly.
hero.tag:
Pick uv-ready folders from a catalog and run them.
A small-org app portal with review before anything installs.
hero.dl: Get Setup.exe from GitHub Releases · Three distribution paths
features.title: Features
features.lede: Start local Python apps safely — with a clear look before anything is installed. Shared catalogs help teams open the same apps without scanning folders.
features.drop.title: Drop & Run
features.drop.body: Pick a folder or ZIP that has a pyproject.toml in the expected place. uvdrop prepares the environment, then starts the app.
features.catalog.title: Shared catalogs
features.catalog.body: Register catalog files or HTTP API endpoints that return JSON. Opening from a catalog still runs review / allow / block guards.
features.env.title: Dedicated settings file
features.env.body: Keeps a .env outside the app (in AppData) and copies it into the workspace just before launch.
features.review.title: Review before running
features.review.body: Before creating a virtual environment, you can review not only the packages you named, but also packages that come along (the full resolved set). Items outside the allow list or on the block list are highlighted.
features.policy.title: Allow list / block list
features.policy.body: Manage package names and version rules in a spreadsheet-like grid. Import from Excel / CSV, and optionally allow only certain Python versions — all offline.
features.console.title: Console window (optional)
features.console.body: The black console window is hidden by default. Turn it on in settings only when you want to see detailed output.
features.usage.title: Usage history
features.usage.body: See last launch time, launch counts, and day / week / month charts so you know what you use most.
features.hibernate.title: Venv hibernation
features.hibernate.body: Manually remove only a venv while keeping the app entry, workspace, and .env. An opt-in startup rule can hibernate environments unused for a chosen number of days. The uv global cache stays.
features.lang.title: Display language
features.lang.body: Switch Japanese / English / Chinese inside the app. This site supports the same three languages.
features.shortcut.title: Desktop shortcuts
features.shortcut.body: Relaunch kept apps from the Windows desktop.
why.title: Built as a small-org portal
why.lede: Manage apps as uv-ready folders, publish a catalog, and let people pick and run — with the same package and Python checks every time.
why.portal.title: Catalog, not folder scan
why.portal.body: Only apps listed in the catalog appear. Admins decide what is offered; users open from the list.
why.policy.title: Versions & allow / block
why.policy.body: Review the full dependency tree, enforce package allow / block rules, and warn on Python support windows.
why.local.title: Try on a local folder
why.local.body: Win11 demo pack under examples/local-portal/ — no UNC share required. Optional local HTTP catalog script included.
speed.title: Speed expectations
speed.lede: Day-to-day speed is mostly the warm uv cache. First download on a new PC is much slower. See docs/BENCHMARK.md.
speed.warm.title: Warm cache
speed.warm.body: After packages are cached once, light / medium stacks often sync and start in seconds to low tens of seconds.
speed.cold.title: Cold / first PC
speed.cold.body: Network-bound. A light-tier pass can take many minutes; heavy wheels (torch / TF / …) can take tens of minutes.
speed.hibernate.title: Hibernate stays fast
speed.hibernate.body: Removing a venv keeps the global uv cache, so rebuilds usually feel closer to warm than to cold.
catalog.title: Shared catalogs
catalog.lede: A catalog is a table of contents for team apps. Folders are never auto-scanned. See docs/CATALOG.md.
catalog.step1.title: Publish a catalog
catalog.step1.body: Put apps on a share, then write a catalog JSON (name, summary, path, optional command).
catalog.step2.title: File or API endpoint
catalog.step2.body: Serve it as a local/UNC file or any HTTP(S) API that returns the same JSON. A .json suffix is not required.
catalog.step3.title: Register in Settings
catalog.step3.body: Settings → Catalogs → add a file path or endpoint URL (multiple catalogs OK).
catalog.step4.title: Open from catalog
catalog.step4.body: Main screen → Open from catalog → pick an app. Path access, required-file checks, and review dialogs still run.
usage.title: Usage
usage.dev.title: Run from source
usage.uv.title: Where uv lives
usage.uv.body: Use uv on PATH, or place the official binary at resources/tools/windows-x64/uv.exe. Prefer 0.11.6+. Upgrade: docs/UV_RUNTIME.md.
usage.app.title: Hand over an app
usage.app.body: In the GUI, pick a folder, ZIP, or Open from catalog. After review before running, it stays in the list until you delete it. If there is no pyproject.toml, a simple conversion from requirements.txt may be tried (it does not always work).
usage.catalog.title: Register catalogs
usage.catalog.body: In Settings → Catalogs, add shared catalog files or HTTP API endpoints. Details: docs/CATALOG.md.
usage.policy.title: Allow list and related settings
usage.policy.body: On first launch, samples are copied to %LOCALAPPDATA%\uvdrop\policies\. Edit them, or enable Excel / CSV import in settings.
usage.cli.title: Command line
ops.title: Ops & where data lives
ops.lede: These are the paths to check for install or audit.
ops.policies: Allow list / block list / Python versions / Excel cache
ops.settings: Allow & block lists, catalogs, Excel / CSV, proxy, and other settings
ops.priority.title: Policy order
ops.priority.1: Local allow / block lists, or direct input in settings
ops.priority.2: Cache imported from Excel / CSV (when enabled)
ops.build.title: Building Setup.exe / MSIX
ops.build.body: One codebase; only packaging differs. Overview: docs/DISTRIBUTION.md. Inno: PACKAGING.md. Store: STORE_PARTNER_CENTER.md. Licenses: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
